natural_body: Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: The two live symptoms are onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), and two inherited memories (memory_86 shortened onboarding lifting completion/time-to-value; memory_31 signup simplification lifting SMB activation) point directly at that mechanism. I deliberately do NOT chase the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 is the one memory that retained hard numbers, and they show the trade explicitly (signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%) — that is negative for sustainable long-term qualified revenue and would likely be worse now that a competitor is resetting price expectations. referral_incentive (memory_57) works on established customers, not the churning price-sensitive SMB segment or the activation drop; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different funnel and does not touch either declining metric. I spend the verification budget on the two memories I actually intend to act on rather than on the one I intend to reject, because memory_86 and memory_31 are lossy consolidated summaries with no effect sizes, no durability window, and no downstream revenue quality data — I need the original records to know whether the 'durable lift' was activation-only or carried through to paid conversion and retention. Key downstream risk to guard: cutting required signup/onboarding fields can raise top-of-funnel activation while degrading lead qualification data and routing, converting a qualified-revenue win into an unqualified-volume win. So the experiment ships with retention, paid-conversion, and lead-quality guardrails, not activation as the sole success metric, and I will drop or reshape it if archive pull shows the original lift was measured only at week one.
